cues.en: Mike: You saw, in the previous video, that a wide range of combinations of hits and false alarms can give rise to exactly the same d-prime.
cues.zh: Mike：上一部影片中，你看到許多不同的命中與誤報組合，都能產生完全相同的 d′。

cues.en: Now, that's not a problem per se, but it does show that d-prime, on its own, captures only part of the signal-detection space.
cues.zh: 這本身並不是問題，但它顯示，單靠 d′ 只能描述訊號偵測空間的一部分。

cues.en: We need to fill out the rest of that signal-detection space, and that's going to be through something called response bias.
cues.zh: 我們需要補足訊號偵測空間的其餘部分，而這要透過所謂的反應偏誤。

cues.en: And that's gonna be the main point of this video.
cues.zh: 這就是這部影片的重點。

cues.en: So let me start by giving an example of two different individuals.
cues.zh: 首先，讓我用兩個不同的人當例子。

cues.en: We have person A and person B.
cues.zh: 我們有 A 和 B 兩個人。

cues.en: Person A is very agreeable.
cues.zh: A 這個人非常隨和。

cues.en: He's really, you know, open-minded.
cues.zh: 他的心胸非常開放。

cues.en: He likes to do lots of stuff, and he likes to say yes often.
cues.zh: 他喜歡做許多事情，而且經常喜歡回答「是」。

cues.en: All the time, as often as possible.
cues.zh: 他總是這樣，能說「是」就說「是」。

cues.en: So that person is gonna have lots of hits, also lots of false alarms, but more hits than false alarms.
cues.zh: 因此，他會有許多命中，也會有許多誤報，但命中比誤報多。

cues.en: And very few misses, and very few correct rejections.
cues.zh: 而漏失和正確拒絕都很少。

cues.en: So that person has a bias towards saying yes, he can still have a high d-prime.
cues.zh: 因此，他偏向回答「是」，但仍然可以有很高的 d′。

cues.en: Now we have our other person, and this is a very disagreeable person, a very conservative, critical, suspicious person.
cues.zh: 現在看看另一個人，他非常不隨和，而且保守、挑剔、多疑。

cues.en: And so this person likes to say no all the time.
cues.zh: 因此，他總是喜歡回答「否」。

cues.en: So he is going to have a lot of misses and a lot of correct rejections.
cues.zh: 所以他會有許多漏失與許多正確拒絕。

cues.en: Not that many hits, but even fewer false alarms.
cues.zh: 命中不多，但誤報更少。

cues.en: So that person can also have a high d-prime.
cues.zh: 因此，他也可以有很高的 d′。

cues.en: So the question is, how do we distinguish between these two people?
cues.zh: 問題是，我們要如何區分這兩個人？

cues.en: They both have high d-primes, the same d-prime, but we know that one person is saying yes really often, and the other person is saying no really often.
cues.zh: 他們的 d′ 都很高，而且數值相同，但我們知道，一個人很常回答「是」，另一個人很常回答「否」。

cues.en: Well, that is exactly what we want to measure.
cues.zh: 這正是我們想測量的事情。

cues.en: We want to measure their bias towards saying yes, or their bias towards saying no.
cues.zh: 我們想測量他們偏向回答「是」或偏向回答「否」的程度。

cues.en: Okay, so that's basically the definition of response bias.
cues.zh: 基本上，這就是反應偏誤的定義。

cues.en: It's the tendency to respond, "Present," or yes, more often, versus the tendency to respond, "Absent," or no, more often.
cues.zh: 也就是更常回答「存在」或「是」的傾向，相對於更常回答「不存在」或「否」的傾向。

cues.en: And again, this is independent to d-prime.
cues.zh: 再次強調，這與 d′ 是獨立的。

cues.en: It has nothing to do with d-prime.
cues.zh: 它與 d′ 無關。

cues.en: Okay, so this is just a rewording of this first statement here.
cues.zh: 這裡只是換個方式表達上面第一句話。

cues.en: And so it's orthogonal to d-prime.
cues.zh: 因此，它與 d′ 正交。

cues.en: It's uncorrelated with d-prime, and that's because very different d-primes can stem from the same bias.
cues.zh: 它與 d′ 不相關，因為非常不同的 d′ 可以來自相同的偏誤。

cues.en: And conversely, we can have very different biases that give rise to exactly the same d-prime value.
cues.zh: 反過來說，非常不同的偏誤也可能產生完全相同的 d′ 值。

cues.en: So here's how we compute the response bias.
cues.zh: 以下是反應偏誤的計算方式。

cues.en: Here is the algorithm.
cues.zh: 這就是演算法。

cues.en: You will see it's really, really similar to how we compute d-prime.
cues.zh: 你會發現，它與計算 d′ 的方式非常、非常相似。

cues.en: In fact, the first two steps are identical to computing d-prime.
cues.zh: 事實上，前兩個步驟與計算 d′ 完全相同。

cues.en: So we can go back to the same example.
cues.zh: 因此，我們可以回到同一個例子。

cues.en: We get the zed value for hits, the zed value for false alarms.
cues.zh: 取得命中的 Z 值，以及誤報的 Z 值。

cues.en: And now the difference is that for bias, computing bias, we don't take the difference between hits and false alarms.
cues.zh: 現在的差別是，在計算偏誤時，我們不是求命中與誤報的差。

cues.en: Instead, we take the average of them.
cues.zh: 而是取兩者的平均值。

cues.en: So we say zed hits plus zed false alarms, divided by 2.
cues.zh: 也就是命中的 Z 值加上誤報的 Z 值，再除以 2。

cues.en: And then there's this convention in the signal-detection theory literature to take the negative of the average.
cues.zh: 接著，訊號偵測理論的文獻有一項慣例，就是取這個平均值的負值。

cues.en: Now, I'm going to explain why taking the average is the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 我會解釋，為什麼取平均值是正確的做法。

cues.en: I don't know how it came to be that we take the negative of the average.
cues.zh: 但我不知道，為什麼最後會採用平均值的負值。

cues.en: You'll see in the next slide, it's a little bit arbitrary.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片中你會看到，這有些任意。

cues.en: It could go either way, but this is the convention, so that's what we all follow.
cues.zh: 兩種方向都可以，但這是慣例，因此大家都遵循它。

cues.en: Now, you might initially be a little bit surprised that we are still only taking into consideration hits and false alarms, and we are not considering in this analysis
cues.zh: 一開始，你可能會有點意外：我們仍然只考慮命中與誤報，在這項分析中沒有考慮

cues.en: the number of times that people actually said no.
cues.zh: 人們實際回答「否」的次數。

cues.en: Is that surprising to you?
cues.zh: 這讓你意外嗎？

cues.en: Well, it shouldn't be, when we think about it more.
cues.zh: 再深入想一想，其實不應該意外。

cues.en: It turns out that, because we are computing proportions here, the number of times that people said no is simply the opposite of the number of times that people said yes.
cues.zh: 因為我們在這裡計算的是比例，所以回答「否」的次數，其實就是回答「是」的次數的另一面。

cues.en: So going back to this example, we can say that, you know, if this number were lower than 0.5, it would mean that people have more misses than hits.
cues.zh: 回到這個例子，如果這個數字小於 0.5，就表示漏失比命中多。

cues.en: And if people had larger than 0.5 here, a proportion higher than 0.5, it would mean that they have more correct rejections than false alarms.
cues.zh: 如果這裡大於 0.5，也就是比例高於 0.5，就表示正確拒絕比誤報多。

cues.en: So just to show that here, you could think of this line here as being the 0.5 dividing line.
cues.zh: 為了在這裡說明，你可以把這條線視為 0.5 的分界線。

cues.en: So if you have more hits than misses, you're gonna have a proportion of hits that is larger than 0.5.
cues.zh: 如果命中比漏失多，命中比例就會大於 0.5。

cues.en: If you have more misses, you'll have a proportion of hits that's smaller than 0.5.
cues.zh: 如果漏失比較多，命中比例就會小於 0.5。

cues.en: Okay, so now I want to explain why averaging the zed scores for these two things is the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 現在我想解釋，為什麼把這兩個量的 Z 分數取平均，是正確的做法。

cues.en: Now, before, we subtracted them, and now we are averaging them together.
cues.zh: 先前我們將兩者相減，現在則是將兩者取平均。

cues.en: So let's also consider that when the proportion here is 0.5, that corresponds to a zed score of exactly zero.
cues.zh: 另外想一想，當這裡的比例是 0.5 時，對應的 Z 分數恰好是零。

cues.en: So when people are saying yes more often than they're saying no, the average, so the proportions of these two quantities are going to be both greater than 0.5.
cues.zh: 因此，當人們回答「是」比回答「否」頻繁時，平均來說，這兩個量的比例都會大於 0.5。

cues.en: So that's gonna put us up here above 0.5.
cues.zh: 所以我們會落在這裡，高於 0.5 的位置。

cues.en: The average is gonna be above 0.5.
cues.zh: 平均值會高於 0.5。

cues.en: That means we have an average zed score that is going to be positive.
cues.zh: 這表示平均 Z 分數會是正的。

cues.en: And then, of course, we attach the minus sign, so that gets flipped.
cues.zh: 當然，接著我們加上負號，因此符號會反轉。

cues.en: Conversely, when people are saying no all the time, then these two proportions are gonna be small, let's say below 0.5.
cues.zh: 反過來，當人們總是回答「否」時，這兩個比例就會很小，比方說低於 0.5。

cues.en: So then their average is going to be negative.
cues.zh: 因此，兩者的平均值就會是負的。

cues.en: And then, again, you know, that gets sign flipped, according to convention.
cues.zh: 同樣地，按照慣例，符號會再反轉。

cues.en: Okay, I hope that makes sense.
cues.zh: 希望這樣說明清楚。

cues.en: So basically, instead of taking the difference between hits and false alarms, we are averaging them together, and we wanna see whether the average here is going to be greater than 0.5 or less than 0.5,
cues.zh: 基本上，我們不是求命中與誤報的差，而是將它們取平均，看看這裡的平均值大於還是小於 0.5，

cues.en: and that gets converted into a zed score that is positive or negative.
cues.zh: 再將它轉換成正或負的 Z 分數。

cues.en: So here is how you interpret the response bias.
cues.zh: 以下是反應偏誤的解讀方式。

cues.en: Now, response bias is a quantity that we can expect to be positive or negative, unlike d-prime, where we don't expect d-prime scores to be smaller than zero.
cues.zh: 反應偏誤是可能為正或為負的量，這與 d′ 不同；我們並不預期 d′ 分數小於零。

cues.en: Okay, so a response bias of zero indicates that people have no response bias, so they're saying yes as often as they're saying no.
cues.zh: 反應偏誤為零，表示沒有反應偏誤，也就是回答「是」和「否」一樣頻繁。

cues.en: And just to come back to this graph here.
cues.zh: 再回到這張圖。

cues.en: So if someone's response bias is zero, it means that they have roughly the same proportion of hits and false alarms, which really means they have the same proportion
cues.zh: 如果某人的反應偏誤為零，表示他的命中與誤報比例大致相同；其實意思是，他的

cues.en: of hits and correct rejections, because the false alarms mirror the correct rejections.
cues.zh: 命中與正確拒絕比例相同，因為誤報與正確拒絕互為鏡像。

cues.en: So when these two quantities are equal, that means that these two quantities will average out to 0.5, which means that you're gonna have, as an average zed score of zero.
cues.zh: 當這兩個量相等時，這兩個量的平均就會是 0.5，也就是平均 Z 分數為零。

cues.en: So a response bias of zero indicates no bias whatsoever.
cues.zh: 因此，反應偏誤為零，表示完全沒有偏誤。

cues.en: People say yes as often as they say no.
cues.zh: 回答「是」與回答「否」一樣頻繁。

cues.en: And then, if we have a positive response bias, it means that people prefer to say no.
cues.zh: 接著，正的反應偏誤表示，人們比較偏好回答「否」。

cues.en: So they're having more misses and correct rejections, and fewer hits and false alarms.
cues.zh: 因此，漏失與正確拒絕比較多，命中與誤報比較少。

cues.en: And conversely, when we have a negative response bias, then it means that people have a bias.
cues.zh: 反過來，負的反應偏誤則表示，人們有一種偏向。

cues.en: They're preferring to say yes, to answer, "Present."
cues.zh: 他們偏好回答「是」，也就是回答「存在」。

cues.en: So that means they're gonna have more hits and false alarms, and fewer misses and correct rejections.
cues.zh: 因此，命中與誤報比較多，漏失與正確拒絕比較少。

cues.en: Now, this is where the minus sign comes in.
cues.zh: 負號就是在這裡發揮作用。

cues.en: So in the last step, we take the average of the zed scores for hits and false alarms, and then we take the average.
cues.zh: 所以最後一步，我們把命中與誤報的 Z 分數取平均，然後再取平均。

cues.en: Now again, you know, I can't justify this decision.
cues.zh: 再次強調，我無法說明這項決定的理由。

cues.en: You know, why do we have negative bias for preferring yes and a positive bias for preferring no?
cues.zh: 為什麼偏好回答「是」是負偏誤，而偏好回答「否」是正偏誤？

cues.en: Someone, you know, must have come up with this a long time ago, like 70 years ago, and it just sort of propagated through the literature, and now that's kind of what is widely accepted.
cues.zh: 一定是很久以前，也許 70 年前，有人提出這個做法，接著在文獻中流傳，成為現在普遍接受的慣例。

cues.en: Okay, so in this video, I introduced you to the concept of response bias, and why we need response bias to help us understand the entire space
cues.zh: 這部影片中，我介紹了反應偏誤的概念，以及為什麼需要反應偏誤，才能幫助我們了解

cues.en: of signal-detection theory.
cues.zh: 訊號偵測理論的完整空間。

cues.en: And it's a complement to the d-prime measure.
cues.zh: 它是 d′ 這項指標的補充。
